nodes.name: Fe electrodeposition on BN cathode
nodes.procedure: The dissolved Fe(III) salt (150 μM initial concentration) in 30 wt% KOH electrolyte is continuously electrodeposited onto bare Ni mesh (BN) cathode surface during constant current electrolysis at 0.4 A cm^{-2}, 60 °C for 48 h, forming porous Fe/Fe (hydr)oxide dendrite layers that progressively increase the electrode surface area.
nodes.source_text: The dissolved Fe will deposit on the cathode... progressive electrodeposition of Fe on the BN surface... formation of Fe dendrite layers that form on the cathode surface.

nodes.name: Dynamic Fe incorporation/leaching on BN anode
nodes.procedure: Dissolved Fe(III) species (initial 150 μM) incorporate into the Ni oxide layer of bare Ni mesh (BN) anode through dynamic equilibrium between incorporation and leaching during constant current OER at 0.4 A cm^{-2}, 60 °C for 48 h in 30 wt% KOH, forming mixed Ni/Fe oxyhydroxide active sites.
nodes.source_text: mechanism based on an equilibrium between leaching and incorporation of Fe onto the oxide layer of the anode... density of OER active sites related to Fe incorporated to the oxide layer.

nodes.name: Fe electrodeposition on RN cathode
nodes.procedure: Dissolved Fe(III) salt deposits on porous RANEY® Ni mesh cathode during constant current HER operation at 0.4 A cm^{-2} for 48 h at 60 °C, forming Fe/Fe (hydr)oxide without blocking initial porous structure.
nodes.source_text: Deposition of Fe/Fe (hydr)oxide onto the porous RN surface is nevertheless confirmed by SEM observation... However, the SEM images show that the deposition of the Fe does not block the initial porous RANEY® layer.
